title: The observation reply
description: The result of an observation and the catalogue of images taken. The images are separate files, and this reply is written atomically, last. A reader judges completeness by the catalogue (frames) being present, the id matching, and the count agreeing — **when the ceiling cut the request, it agrees with the count after cutting**, so checking against the requested count alone reads a complete reply as a failure (the cut appears in warnings). A reply is written even when nothing could be taken, with the reason in warnings (ADR-0018 decision 3).

schemaVersion.description: The version of this reply's format. How it is raised is ADR-0018 decision 5.

id.description: The identifier of the request this answers. A reader knows it is done by this matching.

image.description: The file name of the last image taken, relative to this reply. Omitted when the declared number of shots did not come together, so a reader may treat the absence of this key as failure. Each entry in frames carries its own name, so a reader never has to construct one.

frame.description: The number of the frame this reply was written on. When everything came together, the same as the last frame taken.

time.description: The time of the frame this reply was written on, in seconds.

size.description: The size of the surface that was drawn, in pixels.

warnings.description: Anything that had to be noted while taking the shots. When it failed, the reason is here. An empty array when there is nothing.

stats.description: A summary of the last image taken. **Omitted when the declared number of shots did not come together** — omitted even if some were taken, so the condition is the same as image. Summaries of what was taken up to that point are carried by the entries in frames.

load.description: How hard it is working. Carried so that fast or slow is answered with a number rather than guessed from the picture.

frameRate.description: The frame rate actually coming out just now. Omitted before it can be measured and **while frames have not advanced for a while**, so that a stale number is never named during a stall.

frameTimeMs.description: The interval between recent frames, in milliseconds. Omitted before it can be measured and **while frames have not advanced for a while** (the same condition as frameRate).

memoryMB.description: The physical memory the process is using, in MB. Omitted when it cannot be read.

thermalState.description: The thermal state. A reader should pass an unfamiliar value through rather than drop it, since the range can widen.

values.description: The values the sketch exposed on the frame this reply was written on. Omitted when there are none.

stamp.description: Which generation of input produced this image. Returned exactly as the running side passed it. A reader should compare it for equality as an opaque identifier and depend on neither its meaning nor its length. Omitted when nothing was passed.

frames.description: The catalogue of images taken, in the order they were taken. Present even when a single shot was asked for, as a one-element array, because a reply whose shape changed with the count would make every reader start by telling the shapes apart. When it was cut short, only what was taken appears.

image.description: This image's file name, relative to the reply.

frame.description: The number of the frame this image was drawn on. The same number twice in a row means nothing advanced in between.

time.description: The time of the frame this image was drawn on, in seconds.

stats.description: A summary of this image. Carried so that whether anything moved can be judged without opening the picture.

values.description: The values the sketch exposed on this frame. Omitted when there are none.

stats.description: A summary of an image. Carried so that questions like whether it is entirely black, or crowded into a corner, can be judged without opening the picture. Counted in displayable form, after the output stage. **What omits it differs by where it sits** — an entry in the catalogue (frames) always has one, since it has an image, while at the level above it is omitted under the same condition as image (the declared number of shots did not come together).

meanColor.description: The mean of red, green and blue (0…1).

contentFraction.description: The share of sampled points whose colour differs from the ground, meaning the most common colour (0…1). 0 is a uniform image. **The ground is not the top-left point** — taking the top left as the ground swaps content and ground for any image with something drawn there.

contentBounds.description: The bounding box of the points that carry content. The origin is the top left, normalised by width and height. Omitted when there is not a single point.

sampleGrid.description: The grid of points that were counted. Sampled on this grid rather than over every pixel.

values.description: The values the sketch exposed on this frame, as a type and value pair per name. Omitted when there are none.
